question: Normally, A QWERTY keyboard has ______ keys.
solution:
The correct answer is __**104**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A standard QWERTY keyboard typically has **104 keys**.
 
• The layout includes **alphabetic keys, numeric keys, function keys, and a number pad**.
 
• QWERTY refers to the first six letters on the top row of the alphabetic section on the keyboard.
 
• The **QWERTY layout** was designed in the 1870s by Christopher Sholes, the inventor of the typewriter.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **QWERTY Keyboard**

 
 
• The QWERTY keyboard is the most common modern-day keyboard layout.
 
• It was designed to prevent mechanical jams in early typewriters by spacing out commonly used letter pairings.
 
• Despite the existence of more efficient keyboard layouts (such as Dvorak), QWERTY remains the most popular due to historical adoption.
 
• QWERTY keyboards are used in most English-speaking countries and many other regions worldwide.
 
 
 
• **Function Keys**
 
 
• Function keys are the keys labeled F1 to F12 and are located at the top of the keyboard.
 
• They are used to perform special actions, like refreshing a page (F5) or entering the BIOS setup (F2 or Del).
 
• The specific function of these keys can vary depending on the operating system and the application being used.
 
 
 
• **Numeric Keypad**
 
 
• The numeric keypad is a set of keys on the right side of the keyboard, usually arranged in a grid.
 
• It includes numbers from 0 to 9, basic arithmetic operators, and a decimal point.
 
• It's primarily used for quick data entry and calculations, especially in accounting and finance applications.
